items.excerpt: Mayo Clinic researchers trained an AI model on longitudinal EHR and routine lab data (6,066 patients, 33,396 controls); it reached AUROC 0.853, and a >50% predicted risk meant an 88% chance of diagnosis within a year (ACS Clinical Congress 2026).
items.title: AI model predicts pancreatic cancer risk 3 years before diagnosis

items.excerpt: Barcelona Supercomputing Center built MCP servers linking AI agents to NeKo, MaBoSS and PhysiCell so researchers can build tumor digital twins by natural-language conversation, producing model drafts in under 10 minutes instead of months (npj Systems Biology and Applications).
items.title: Tumor digital twins: from months to minutes with AI

items.excerpt: Sungkyunkwan University's 4D fMRI CrossFormer, a lightweight vision transformer learning spatial and temporal brain activity jointly, detected Alzheimer's disease at a 96.28% F1 score and maps the regions driving each prediction (IEEE JBHI).
items.title: New AI method for brain disorder screening (4D fMRI CrossFormer)

items.excerpt: UW-Madison researchers trained a machine-learning model on high-throughput phage mutation data; it predicted mutations that let bacteriophages infect hosts up to a million times more effectively, validated in the lab (Cell Systems).
items.title: AI-guided mutations help viruses infect bacteria up to 1 million times more effectively

items.excerpt: Duke-NUS and SMU researchers propose in Nature Human Behaviour that isolated people substitute AI companions for human contact, risking 'social deskilling', while well-connected users use them as a supplement, a rich-get-richer dynamic.
items.title: AI companions may erode social skills among isolated users, framework suggests

items.excerpt: UW-Madison designed quantum nanostructures with vacancy color centers that give optical neural networks strong nonlinearity at power seven orders of magnitude below conventional optical materials (Nature Communications).
items.title: Tiny quantum nanostructures could make AI less of an energy hog

items.excerpt: UC Riverside found LLM confidence and correctness live in distinct internal features; suppressing features tied to uncertainty and error flags unreliable answers, lifting accuracy on retained questions from 62% to 81% (arXiv).
items.title: Making AI more trustworthy by making it red-flag its own doubtful answers

items.excerpt: A University of Michigan study of 482 adults found chatbot agreement boosted confidence, but disagreement did not change minds; instead users judged the AI as machine-like and less likely to consult it again (Computers in Human Behavior Reports).
items.title: When AI disagrees, people change how they perceive the technology, not their original view

items.excerpt: NUS engineers built reconfigurable MoS2 transistors that switch between image filtering and spiking-neural-network roles, cutting active hardware blocks ~36% with accuracy within 0.3 points (Nature Electronics).
items.title: AI hardware design could filter out irrelevant visual data to reduce energy use

items.excerpt: OpenAI's AI-assisted Navier-Stokes proof seems eligible for the $1-million Millennium Prize, but only via a controversial loophole, mathematicians argue.
items.title: Did OpenAI solve the wrong Navier-Stokes problem?

items.excerpt: The brain runs on roughly a lightbulb's wattage; neuromorphic computing researchers are chasing that efficiency for AI.
items.title: Could brain-inspired computers run on the same amount of power as a human brain?

items.excerpt: A Stanford arXiv preprint builds an AI that runs 'mental simulations' (a learned world model) to plan spacecraft rendezvous and docking, instead of relying only on hard-coded orbital equations and human pilots.
items.title: Stanford Engineers Teach Spacecraft to 'Dream' Their Way to the Space Station

items.excerpt: QC Design says its Meridian AI system achieved more than 10x lower logical error rates than published methods across 100+ quantum-computer design tasks.
items.title: QC Design Reports 10x Logical Error Reduction With Meridian AI

items.excerpt: IonQ researchers tested a quantum generative machine-learning model for change detection in Capella Space SAR imagery, beating a classical baseline in some conditions, on a simulator and a trapped-ion QPU.
items.title: Evaluating Quantum Generative Models on Real Satellite Radar

items.excerpt: University of Washington students stress-tested Ai2's AutoDiscovery, showing AI can surface promising scientific leads while human judgment and rigorous validation matter more.
items.title: Teaching future scientists to interrogate AI tools for scientific discovery

items.excerpt: Generative AI and papermills are flooding journals with fraudulent papers, and publishers are responding with new detection tools and integrity checks.
items.title: How scientific publishers are fighting back against fraudulent papermills

items.excerpt: A new wave of radiology practices is embracing AI aggressively, developing and deploying models in-house. (STAT+ paywalled)
items.title: In radiology, AI is blurring the line between technology development and clinical practice

items.excerpt: Shifting from instant AI responses back to listening, patience and shared attention with people takes longer than closing a chat window.
items.title: From Working With AI to Connecting With People
